cards.back: A combination of computer hardware and software designed to perform a specific function, often as part of a larger system.

cards.front: What are the main parts of an embedded system?
cards.back: Hardware (physical electronic parts), Software (programs), and Firmware (low-level software stored in memory that controls the device).
Low-level software that directly controls a device's hardware and is usually stored in memory.

cards.front: What is the basic flow of an embedded system?
cards.back: Input/Sensor → Converter → Processor → Output/Actuator

cards.front: What is the difference between a microprocessor and a microcontroller?
cards.back: A microprocessor usually needs separate memory and peripheral circuits. A microcontroller is a small computer on one chip that includes a processor, memory, and peripheral interfaces.

cards.front: What is a System on a Chip (SoC)?
cards.back: A chip that contains several processors and interfaces on one single chip.
Field-Programmable Gate Array — an integrated circuit that can be configured to perform different functions. It is flexible.
Application-Specific Integrated Circuit — a chip designed for a specific function. Efficient when the function is known and will not change.
Converts physical information (temperature, pressure, motion) into an electrical signal.
Produces or controls a physical action or output. Common examples: motors and solenoids.
Changes an analog signal into a digital signal so the processor can understand it.
Changes digital data back into an analog signal for output.

cards.front: What is a real-time embedded system?
cards.back: A system that must produce the required output within a defined time limit.
Real-Time Operating System — helps control software execution and communication with hardware according to timing rules. Not every embedded system needs one.

cards.front: What are the characteristics of embedded systems?
cards.back: Task-specific, made of hardware/software/firmware, can be part of a larger system, use microprocessors or microcontrollers, often used for sensing and real-time computing in IoT, range from simple to complex, may need to complete tasks within a time limit.

cards.front: What are the types of embedded systems by scale?
cards.back: Small-scale (8-bit MCU), Medium-scale (16-32 bit MCUs), Sophisticated-scale (complex hardware, software, algorithms).

cards.front: What are the four embedded software architectures?
cards.back: Simple control loop, Interrupt-controlled system, Cooperative multitasking, Preemptive multitasking/multithreading.

cards.front: What are the three types of embedded systems by portability?
cards.back: Mobile (small, portable), Networked (connected to a network), Standalone (performs specialized task independently).
A Google product that helps developers build, manage, and grow applications. It provides ready-made services for Android, iOS, web, and Unity apps, plus cloud storage and NoSQL databases.
A type of database that does not require traditional table-based (SQL) organization.

cards.front: What is the Firebase Realtime Database?
cards.back: A cloud-based NoSQL database that can quickly manage and synchronize data in real time. Similar to a large JSON file.
A NoSQL document database that stores information in documents with key-value pairs.
A service that checks the identity of a user. Firebase provides tools that make user authentication easier to build and maintain.
Allows developers to remotely change certain application settings, interface components, or behavior without pushing an app update.
Provides a connection between applications and users for sending and receiving messages and notifications.
A Firebase service that provides real-time crash reports and details to help developers find and understand application problems.
Provides information about application performance so developers can review problems and make improvements.
Allows developers to provide pre-release applications to trusted testers for testing and feedback.

cards.front: What is Google Analytics in Firebase?
cards.back: Provides information about application usage and user engagement. It measures actions or events within an application.
Uses machine learning with app analytics data to create user segments based on behavior and support other Firebase features.
Used to direct users to specific content inside an application.
Compares different versions of an application experience to help determine which version works better.

cards.front: What are the three main Firebase feature groups?
cards.back: Build Better Applications (Realtime DB, Firestore, Auth, Remote Config, FCM), Improve App Quality (Crashlytics, Performance Monitoring, App Distribution), Grow Your App (Analytics, Predictions, Dynamic Links, A/B Testing).
Application Programming Interface — allows two applications to communicate with each other. A bridge between software applications.

cards.front: What is a disadvantage of Firebase?
cards.back: NoSQL may be difficult for people who are used to SQL databases.
James Tamplin and Andrew Lee. It began with an online chat service called Envolve. The modern Firebase architecture emerged around 2012.
The brain of an embedded system. It is the basic unit that takes inputs and produces an output after processing data.

cards.front: What are the main units of a processor?
cards.back: Control Unit (CU) — fetches instructions from memory. Execution Unit (EU) — contains the ALU and carries out data transfer, conversion, and program control tasks.
A processor repeatedly fetches and executes instructions in the same order they are fetched from memory.

cards.front: What is a General Purpose Processor (GPP)?
cards.back: A processor designed to execute a wide range of tasks with a flexible instruction set architecture (ISA) and typically a large amount of memory. Used in PCs, workstations, servers, routers, and switches.

cards.front: What are the three main types of instructions for a GPP?
cards.back: Arithmetic (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV), Logical (AND, OR, XOR, NOT), and Control (JUMP, LOOP, RET, HALT).
A single VLSI chip containing a CPU. It may include caches, a floating-point unit, and pipelining units. Generally needs separate memory and peripherals.

A single-chip VLSI unit (microcomputer) with limited computational power but enhanced I/O capability, on-chip program memory, and several functional units. Widely used in embedded systems for real-time control.
Appliances, industrial control systems, toys, medical devices, automotive systems, telecommunications equipment.
A microprocessor designed specifically for the needs of an embedded system. Small, power-efficient, and often integrates peripherals to save power.

cards.front: What is a DSP (Digital Signal Processor)?
cards.back: A special-purpose embedded processor built for the computational and power demands of audio, video, and communication applications. It measures, filters, and compresses digital or analog signals.
Speech processing, image processing, medical processing, seismology, and radar.
Mostly used as an image or video processor. A microprocessor-based SoC designed to handle digital streaming data in real time. Considered a class of DSP.
Application-Specific Standard Product — an integrated circuit dedicated to a specific application market and sold to more than one user. Combines digital, mixed-signal, and analog products.
Application-Specific Instruction Processor — usually used in a SoC. Has a minimum ISA and configurable logic for building a custom instruction set.

cards.front: What is the difference between an ASSP and an ASIC?
cards.back: An ASSP is sold to multiple users in a specific market. When the same chip is sold to a single user, it is considered an ASIC.

cards.front: What are the two main parts of embedded system architecture?
cards.back: Embedded hardware (processor, memory, bus, peripherals, I/O ports, controllers) and Embedded software (operating system and applications).
Also called Princeton architecture. Software and data share the same memory and bus. 'The program is data, and the data is the program.'

cards.front: What is the Von Neumann bottleneck?
cards.back: A performance limitation caused by instructions and data sharing the same bus for transmission. Cache and branch-prediction technology can help address it.
Architecture with two separate memory modules and two independent buses — one for instructions and one for data. They do not coexist in the same module.

cards.front: Which architecture is better suited for DSP and why?
cards.back: Harvard architecture — because separate instruction and data memory provides greater data-memory bandwidth, making it well suited for digital signal processing.

cards.front: What is the main practical difference between Von Neumann and Harvard in modern processors?
cards.back: Harvard splits L1 cache into I-cache (instruction cache) and D-cache (data cache), while Von Neumann uses a single cache.

Reduced Instruction Set Computer — uses a small, limited, simple instruction set. Each instruction has a standard word length and short execution time. Uses many general-purpose registers to compensate.
Complex Instruction Set Computer — features a powerful instruction set with different instruction lengths, which facilitates pipelined execution.

cards.front: How has the line between RISC and CISC blurred?
cards.back: Many CISC processors (like Intel x86) now translate instructions into RISC-like micro-ops through a decoder, gaining RISC-style efficiency internally.
A processor's internal instruction execution unit, decoded from a macro operation (the original x86 instruction).
Combining multiple macro operations into a single micro operation for efficiency. For example, x86 CMP and JMP can fuse into a single compare-and-jump micro-op.

cards.front: Name the 5 common embedded microprocessor architectures.
cards.back: RISC, CISC, MIPS, PowerPC, and SuperH.
